title: Heart sounds and the ECG
summary: The heart sounds (a phonocardiogram) recorded with an ECG.
description: The heart sounds were recorded with an electronic stethoscope on the chest (a phonocardiogram, PCG) at the same time as an ECG. The first heart sound (S1) comes as the atrioventricular valves close at the start of ventricular systole, just after the QRS; the second (S2) as the aortic and pulmonary valves close at the end of systole, near the end of the T wave. The starts of the sounds were marked by hand. Switch on Sound and press Play to listen (headphones help).
look_for: S1 just after the QRS, and S2 near the end of the T wave
Systole (S1 to S2) and diastole (S2 to the next S1): which is longer at rest?
Which sound is louder at this place on the chest?

beats.note: The beats were found automatically by the workbench (the R waves of ECG), and checked by eye, but not by a cardiologist.
